thesis: Kird Ape was an early lesson that a one-mana creature could quietly demand two colors and reward the deck with statistics far above the normal rate.

canonicalIdentity.currentOracleText: This creature gets +1/+2 as long as you control a Forest.

competitiveTimeline.significance: Its record runs from the earliest red-green decks and the first World Championship through Extended and Legacy Zoo, establishing the model later one-drops would refine.

playbook.role: Lead with Kird Ape only when the mana base can supply a Forest quickly; Taiga and later dual-land structures turn the apparent red one-drop into a dependable 2/3. Sequence fetches and shock lands so the bonus is active before combat.

claims.summary: Kird Ape was an early lesson that a one-mana creature could quietly demand two colors and reward the deck with statistics far above the normal rate.
Taiga both casts the red Ape and satisfies its Forest condition, making it 2/3; mentioning Forest does not change red Commander color identity.
The official 1994 Worlds retrospective publishes Lestree’s Ape list and documents his runner-up finish.
In 2003 Rosewater acknowledged that banning Kird Ape at the start of Extended had been a mistake; the article no longer invents a policy rationale.
